findings.whyThisIsNotPedantry: The artifact itself treats exactByteIntent and passProperty as two distinct named fields — it distinguishes them correctly in its own per-state source records, 12 against 1. Because the artifact draws that distinction internally, the top-level 'from live G01 v1 exactByteIntent' cannot be read as loose shorthand for the harness as a whole; it is a field-level claim, and for one state it is wrong. The misattribution is also itemised rather than incidental: whatIsAuthored spells out 'defaultInstall.excludes membership' as the last member of a list introduced by the exactByteIntent header, so the one item that does not come from that field is named explicitly inside it.
findings.whatIsNotWrong: The exclusion state is genuinely drawn from live occupancy — passProperty sits in the same pinned v1 file at the same digest — and its own stateNamed is an exact substring of passProperty. So the substantive form of the prompt's attack fails: no named state is invented and none comes from outside the pinned occupancy. This finding is about provenance precision, not content, and nothing prohibited is authored by it.
findings.consequence: The prompt's own attack line is 'named states are not drawn from live occupancy exactByteIntent'. Checked mechanically against the artifact's three top-level attributions, one named state is not, and a reader who trusts whatIsAuthored would look for defaultInstall.excludes in exactByteIntent and not find it. This is the same defect class as CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1 earlier in this very chain, where an authorityClaim stated a provenance that did not hold on the bytes.
findings.fix: Either attribute to both fields in the three top-level locations — 'drawn from live G01 v1 exactByteIntent and passProperty' — or move 'defaultInstall.excludes membership' out of the exactByteIntent enumeration in whatIsAuthored and name its passProperty source there, as initialStates[12] already does correctly.
findings.notRequested: This fix requires no new bytes, no D-006 unit, no threshold, and no change to any named state.

observationsNotFindings: The 'Per platform:' prefix in exactByteIntent grammatically introduces all seven items — artifact bytes, sha256, raw byte count, the D-006 numeral, signature set, SBOM and published artifact list — but the subject expands only the first two per platform and names the remaining ones once globally. I did not charge this. At least one listed item, the D-006 numeral 25 MB, is manifestly a single threshold constant and cannot be per-platform, so 'Per platform:' demonstrably does not distribute over the whole list, and the subject's split is a defensible reading. It also makes no exhaustiveness claim — purpose says 'naming initial states', not every initial state — and whatIsAuthored discloses the split openly. A later fixture cycle still has the pinned source to read for whether signature sets and SBOMs are per platform, so nothing is left undecidable. Worth noting only because the source prose is genuinely ambiguous on that point and the subject resolves it silently.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: Custody is clean: the subject matches the dispatched digest at start and end, 8910 bytes, mode 0444, unmoved, at HEAD 5d5d778, and all three cited digests recompute. The strongest attack available here was that the pinned occupancy is the wrong G01 version, since v3 exists and is later — it fails on the bytes, because all three extractions carry artifactPathWhenAuthored = the v1 path, so v1 is the file that sits at the promised path, and the subject's role note cites my own CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1 accurately in saying so. The D-006 trap is fully avoided and avoided well: MiB, mebibyte, megabyte, 1048576 and 1024 all return zero, all nine occurrences of 26214400 are negations read individually, and the unit's UNDECIDED standing is carried into the state id itself. The four platform names, which exactByteIntent never enumerates, trace exactly to live D-002's 'macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux (x86_64, arm64)'. The 'leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded is empty' claim was resolved rather than accepted, and the live accepted parent does carry an empty array. What lands is narrow and is not about content: authorityClaim, purpose and whatIsAuthored all attribute the named states to live G01 v1 exactByteIntent, but the exclusion state comes from passProperty — 'defaultInstall' and 'excludes' occur nowhere in exactByteIntent — and whatIsAuthored itemises 'defaultInstall.excludes membership' inside the exactByteIntent list. The artifact distinguishes the two fields correctly in its own per-state source records, 12 against 1, which is exactly what stops this being read as loose shorthand. It is the same provenance-honesty class as CLAUDE-G01H-V3-SF1 earlier in this chain. The fix is a wording correction in three places and requires no new bytes. 18 attacks run, 17 refuted, one landing.
